Thursday, October 29

Game recap

PHI2WSH5Final: PHI 2, WSH 5

Dylan Strome handed out treats a few days early: three assists, all of them gift-wrapped for Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou in a 5-2 Capitals win over Philadelphia. Tuch opened the scoring 1:50 in and closed it with an empty-netter, two goals on the night. Kyrou also scored twice, a power-play goal in the second and the one that put Washington back up two after Matvei Michkov's power-play goal made it 3-2 midway through the third. Sean Couturier had the other Flyers goal, and Aliaksei Protas got his first of the season. Logan Thompson stopped 23 of 25; Joseph Woll stopped 25 of 29. Matt Roy threw nine hits and still found time for an assist. Washington is 7-4-0. Philadelphia is 3-8-4, and two goals is starting to look less like a bad night and more like the ceiling.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY0EDM4Final: CGY 0, EDM 4

The Battle of Alberta lasted about one period. Mathieu Joseph scored at 7:46 of the first off a Connor McDavid feed, Mattias Ekholm made it 2-0 in the second, and then Edmonton scored twice in 21 seconds early in the third: Kasperi Kapanen on the power play and Alex Formenton right behind him. McDavid and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins had two assists each, and Tristan Jarry stopped all 24 shots for the shutout. Calgary tried a goalie change after the first, with Devin Cooley (8 saves on 9) giving way to Dustin Wolf (20 on 23), which fixed nothing because the problem was at the other end. Ty Emberson and Brennan Othmann dropped the gloves in the first. Edmonton is 9-2-2. Calgary is 5-7-0 and used two goalies and zero goals, which is a lot of equipment for a night with nothing to show for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD2COL5Final: NJD 2, COL 5

Connor Brown scored both New Jersey goals, including an unassisted shorthanded one in the first, and the Devils still got run over 5-2 in Denver. Colorado scored five straight: Gabriel Landeskog tied it on the power play in the second, then Nazem Kadri, Parker Kelly, Nathan MacKinnon and Jaden Schwartz piled on in the third, the last two 30 seconds apart. Brent Burns and Sam Malinski had two assists each, and Kadri and Schwartz had a goal and an assist. The Avalanche outshot New Jersey 44-22; Jake Allen made 39 saves, Mackenzie Blackwood 20. Colorado is 7-5-1. New Jersey is 8-5-0, and after trading for a Vezina goalie last week, the 44 shots suggest the next phone call should be about the defense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR4SEA5Final: TOR 4, SEA 5

Toronto did the hard part and then forgot to finish. Down 4-2 in the third, the Leafs got one from Jack Roslovic and a 6-on-5 tying goal from Auston Matthews with 1:30 left, and then Brandon Montour won it for Seattle with 33 seconds to go, 5-4. Gavin McKenna had his first two-goal game, both on the power play, plus an assist; Matthews had a goal and two assists. Seattle spread it around: Berkly Catton, Josh Mahura with his first of the season, Chandler Stephenson on the power play, Ryker Evans and Montour, with Mackie Samoskevich adding two assists. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 12 of 17; Philipp Grubauer 18 of 22. Cale Fleury and Vinni Lettieri fought in the second. Seattle is 8-4-1. Toronto is 7-6-2 and erased a two-goal deficit only to lose in the last minute, which is the most Maple Leafs sentence ever written.

Wednesday, October 28

Game recap

CBJ4PHI3OTFinal: CBJ 4, PHI 3 OT

Columbus scored three goals in 2:46 of the first period, then spent the next 40 minutes trying to give them back, and the Flyers almost took the gift. Adam Fantilli, Kent Johnson and Denton Mateychuk built the 3-0 lead on a Dan Vladar who finished with 11 saves on 15 shots, which is a lot of goals for a team that only managed 15 shots all night. Noah Cates and Trevor Zegras chipped away, and Jamie Drysdale tied it with the goalie pulled and 11 seconds left. Then Johnson, with two goals and an assist, ended it 2:22 into overtime. Cam Talbot made 28 saves for the Blue Jackets. Philadelphia outshot Columbus 31-15 and still lost, now 0-3 in 3-on-3 overtime, the hockey version of running a marathon and missing the finish line by a step. The Flyers keep finding new ways to lose, and they're getting creative about it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS1CAR2Final: BOS 1, CAR 2

The Bruins scored 91 seconds in, on a Pavel Zacha power-play goal, and then apparently decided that was plenty. Boston managed 15 shots all night. Carolina had 30, and Jeremy Swayman (28 saves) kept it close until the Hurricanes finally solved him. Jackson Blake tied it with 52 seconds left in the first, and Sebastian Aho put home his eighth of the season at 10:19 of the third for the winner. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 14 saves, which is basically a paid night off. Nicolas Deslauriers and Tanner Jeannot dropped the gloves in the first for the evening's other entertainment, and Mark Jankowski returned to the Carolina lineup. The Hurricanes move to 10-2-2. The Bruins are 9-3-1 and still good, but 15 shots against a top team is a business trip where you forget your laptop.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK1CHI2Final: LAK 1, CHI 2

Chicago snapped a three-game losing streak, and it took a defenseman scoring his first of the year to do it. Samuel Helenius gave the Kings an early lead with his first goal of the season at 2:31, and Los Angeles then went the final 57 minutes without another one. Roman Kantserov tied it on a second-period power play off a Connor Bedard feed, and Wyatt Kaiser won it at 7:17 of the third, from Frank Nazar and Patrick Kane. Spencer Knight was excellent with 25 saves on 26 shots; Anton Forsberg made 25 at the other end. Quinton Byfield fired six shots and Artemi Panarin played nearly 24 minutes without a point. The Blackhawks improve to 4-8-0. The Kings fall to 3-6-2 with one goal from their fourth line and none from anybody paid to score them.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL2STL0Final: MTL 2, STL 0

Jacob Fowler stopped all 46 shots the Blues threw at him, and St. Louis threw just about everything, the rink's spare pucks included. Philip Broberg had six shots, four other Blues had five each, and none of them got one past Fowler. The Canadiens needed only 20 shots of their own. Zachary Bolduc scored in the second period, Florian Xhekaj got his first of the season early in the third, and Mike Matheson assisted on both. Jordan Binnington made 18 saves and still took the loss, which won't help a goalie already sitting on the trade boards. Montreal is 7-3-2. The Blues fall to 5-6-1 after outshooting a team 46-20 and getting shut out, and at some point they have to stop blaming the goalie and start blaming the aim.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI4NSH3SOFinal: NYI 4, NSH 3 SO

The Islanders led 3-0 eight minutes into the second period, and Nashville spent the rest of regulation proving that no lead in Music City is safe. Anthony Duclair, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat built it; Filip Forsberg (power play), Alexander Kerfoot and Ryan O'Reilly erased it, O'Reilly tying the game 4:16 into the third. Overtime solved nothing, though Matthew Schaefer played all of it and finished with 32:16 of ice time, the kind of workload usually reserved for a veteran. In the shootout Kyle Palmieri and Horvat scored, while O'Reilly and Forsberg both missed. Semyon Varlamov made 20 saves; Juuse Saros made 25. New York is 6-4-2. The Predators are 4-3-5, a team so committed to the loser point it should hang a banner for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD5DAL1Final: NJD 5, DAL 1

Connor Hellebuyck's Devils debut was about as stressful as a warm bath: 17 saves on 18 shots, with the skaters in front of him doing everything else. Nico Hischier scored twice, opening the night at 2:41 and adding another 38 seconds into the second. Jesper Boqvist, Luke Hughes and Jack Hughes did the rest, and the Hughes brothers each had a goal. Justin Hryckowian got Dallas its only goal. Jamie Benn and Brenden Dillon fought in the second period, which was the closest the Stars came to winning anything. Casey DeSmith allowed five goals on 27 shots. New Jersey has won four straight and is 8-4-0. Dallas falls to 7-4-1 and looked like a team that had read about Hellebuyck all week and decided not to bother him.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA5WPG1Final: FLA 5, WPG 1

Florida was up 3-0 before the 11-minute mark, and Winnipeg's penalty kill treated the Panthers' power play like a guest of honour. Carter Verhaeghe scored twice on the power play, Niko Mikkola added one in between, and Sam Reinhart made it three power-play goals on the night in the second. Brady Tkachuk finished it in the third, with brother Matthew assisting for his fourth helper of the night. Seth Jones had three assists. Adam Lowry's shorthanded goal was the only thing Jets fans got to cheer. Akira Schmid made 24 saves; Clay Stevenson allowed five on 24 shots. The Panthers are 7-4-2. The Jets are 4-5-3, and a penalty kill that leaky makes every Florida trip to the box look like a free shift.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN3UTA1Final: MIN 3, UTA 1

Three fights and two power-play goals: the Wild brought both the fists and the finish to Utah. Liam O'Brien and Michael McCarron fought in the first, Mikhail Sergachev and Matt Boldy went 88 seconds later, and Vincent Trocheck and Danila Yurov added a third in the second. When the hockey broke out, Minnesota's power play did the damage. Joel Eriksson Ek scored in the second and Kirill Kaprizov got his 14th of the season 48 seconds into the third, both with Quinn Hughes assisting. Maxim Shabanov made it 3-0, and Logan Cooley's late 6-on-5 goal only spoiled the shutout. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves; Karel Vejmelka made 27. The Wild are 9-3-2. Utah is 8-5-0 and learned that winning the fights doesn't count on the scoreboard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT1VGK4Final: OTT 1, VGK 4

For almost 40 minutes nobody scored; then Vegas remembered it's the house. Braeden Bowman scored on the power play with 11 seconds left in the second, Shane Pinto answered on a power play 34 seconds into the third, and Raphael Lavoie scored his first of the season at 8:01 for the winner. William Karlsson and Jack Eichel then added empty-netters, which turns a nervy 2-1 into a 4-1 final. Adin Hill was sharp with 25 saves on 26 shots, and Jonas Johansson matched him with 25 of 27 before the empty net did the rest. Mitch Marner had an assist on Karlsson's goal. Vegas is 9-4-1. The Senators fall to 8-5-0 and flew all that way to learn the Vegas lesson: you can stay at the table a long time, but you don't walk out ahead.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN6ANA5OTFinal: VAN 6, ANA 5 OT

The Canucks hadn't won in double-digit games, trailed 5-2 with under eight minutes left, and somehow won. Anaheim had this one framed: A.J. Greer scored twice, Jeff Malott, Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson piled on, and it was 4-1 after two. Then Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak scored, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored twice with the goalie pulled, at 17:14 and 18:03, to tie it. Filip Hronek won it on a power play 4:49 into overtime, his first of the season. Lukas Dostal allowed six on 33 shots; Leevi Meriläinen gave up five on 23 and still got the win. Vancouver is 3-10-1. The Ducks are 5-6-1 and found the one way to lose to a team that had forgotten how to win: give up four goals in the last 12 minutes of hockey.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF2SJS0Final: BUF 2, SJS 0

Yaroslav Askarov stopped 38 of 39 shots and lost, which is the San Jose experience in one sentence. Olen Zellweger scored 50 seconds into the second period, and that was the only puck anybody got past Askarov all night. Zach Benson's first of the season went into an empty net with 55 seconds left. At the other end Colten Ellis was barely needed and perfect when he was, stopping all 23 shots for the shutout. Owen Power assisted on both Buffalo goals. The Sabres improve to 5-4-3. The Sharks fall to 6-6-1 after getting outshot 39-23 at home, and a rebuild that leaves its best player stopping 38 shots alone is a rebuild that still has a long way to go.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Tuesday, October 27

Game recap

LAK6NYR3Final: LAK 6, NYR 3

The Rangers signed James Reimer on Sunday, started him Monday, and pulled him after one period. Welcome to Broadway, here's your hook. The Kings scored three times on Reimer's first eight shots: Taylor Ward 75 seconds in, Brandt Clarke with an extra attacker, and Drew Doughty late in the first. Dylan Garand came on and gave up two more in the second, Artemi Panarin on the power play back at the Garden and Mikey Anderson, and it was 5-1 before New York found a pulse. Doughty finished with a goal and two assists, Joel Edmundson added a goal and an assist with the empty-netter, and Darcy Kuemper made 23 saves on 26 shots. J.T. Miller, Adam Fox (his first goal after 16 points that were all assists) and Tye Kartye scored for the Rangers, who are 7-6-1 and have lost three straight. Los Angeles had won two games all season before this; New York made it look like a bye week.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR2CGY5Final: TOR 2, CGY 5

The Leafs strolled into Calgary on a four-game win streak and left with a 5-2 loss and a fight story. Matvei Gridin scored twice, once on a power play 25 seconds into the second, and set up another, and Mikael Backlund came back from a two-game absence to score the second goal. It was 3-0 before Toronto showed up. Easton Cowan and William Nylander got it to 3-2 with 14 minutes left, but Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil hit the empty net 46 seconds apart. Devin Cooley made 26 saves on 28 in his fourth straight start, Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 29 of 32, and Zack MacEwen and Jake Middleton fought in the first. Calgary has won four straight and is 5-6-0. Toronto drops to 7-5-2, proof that a hot streak in October lasts about as long as a Leafs playoff lead.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET4EDM3SOFinal: DET 4, EDM 3 SO

Michal Postava's first NHL start came in Edmonton against Connor McDavid, and he went 3-for-3 in the shootout against McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins. Some guys get a soft debut in Columbus. The Oilers led three times: Vasily Podkolzin in the first, Isaac Howard on the power play in the third and Colton Dach with 3:28 left. Detroit answered every time, through Viktor Arvidsson on the power play, Emmitt Finnie 30 seconds after Howard, and Dylan Larkin with the goalie pulled and 1:17 left, the man in every trade rumor making the play of the night. Lucas Raymond had two assists and scored the only shootout goal, Postava made 25 saves on 28, and Tristan Jarry stopped 26 of 29. Detroit is 5-4-3. Edmonton is 8-2-2 and found out that a lead with McDavid on the ice still isn't safe from its own defense.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, October 26

Game recap

FLA3CHI2Final: FLA 3, CHI 2

Chicago scored 2:34 in, tied it in the second, and still found a way to lose, because that's the brand. Ryan Greene opened it from Mangiapane and Korchinski, Sandis Vilmanis answered, and Matthew Tkachuk put Florida ahead on the power play in the first. Roman Kantserov tied it at 2 in the second off a Kane-and-Bedard setup, the kind of play Chicago has been promising since the draft lottery. Then Lars Eller, of all people, scored the winner with 2:23 left, from Aaron Ekblad. Florida outshot Chicago 33-21; Akira Schmid made 19 saves and Spencer Knight 30. The Panthers are 6-4-2. The Blackhawks are 3-8-0 with three straight losses, and the only thing they're building faster than the rebuild is the losing streak.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI3DAL6Final: NYI 3, DAL 6

The Islanders hung around for 40 minutes, answering every Dallas goal, then the third period showed up and the Stars ran them out of Texas. It was 3-3 after two, with Matthew Schaefer, Kyle Palmieri and Brayden Schenn scoring for New York, before Wyatt Johnston, Jason Robertson and Mikko Rantanen scored in the first 13:02 of the third. Robertson had two, Tyler Seguin a goal and an assist, and Justin Hryckowian got his first of the season on the power play. Dallas outshot New York 38-20; Jake Oettinger made 17 saves and Ilya Sorokin 32 on 38. The Stars have won five straight and sit at 7-3-1. The Islanders are 5-4-2, and they're learning that keeping it close for two periods counts for exactly as much as a moral victory in the standings.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL2WPG1Final: MTL 2, WPG 1

Winnipeg threw 34 shots at Jacob Fowler and got one past him, which is the hockey version of buying 34 lottery tickets and winning a free coffee. Montreal's defensemen did the scoring: Lane Hutson at 7:19 of the second from Noah Dobson and Cole Caufield, then Kaiden Guhle 3:45 later, with Caufield setting him up again. Isak Rosen scored his first of the season with 4:36 left to make it interesting, and that was it. Fowler made 33 saves; Stuart Skinner stopped 19 of 21 at the other end. The Canadiens are 6-3-2 with two straight wins. The Jets are 4-4-3 and scoring 2.45 goals a game, and a team that just traded its franchise goalie can't afford a power outage this long.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL2NSH6Final: COL 2, NSH 6

Colorado spent Sunday night in the penalty box handing out power-play goals like party favors, and Nashville took four of them. The Predators were up 5-0 before the second intermission: Filip Forsberg on the power play, Steven Stamkos, Ryan O'Reilly on the power play, Jack Drury, and O'Reilly again with the extra man. Artturi Lehkonen (his 10th) and Devon Toews scored for Colorado, and Stamkos closed it on a fourth power-play goal. O'Reilly and Stamkos had two each and Roman Josi three assists. Parker Kelly and Jayden Struble fought in the second. Justus Annunen made 19 saves; Scott Wedgewood allowed six on 35. Nashville is 4-3-4. Colorado is 6-5-1 and 4-5-1 in its last 10, and a team built to win the Cup is killing penalties like it's never seen one before.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN4VAN2Final: MIN 4, VAN 2

Quinn Hughes came back to Vancouver, heard the boos, and scored anyway, a power-play goal for his 500th career point, plus an assist for 501. Maxim Shabanov opened it on the power play, Bobby Brink scored his first of the season, and Kirill Kaprizov added his 13th early in the third to make it 4-0. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser scored late for Vancouver, which is a nice way of saying the Canucks woke up after the game was over. Calvin Pickard made 16 saves on 18 shots for his first win with the Wild; Leevi Meriläinen stopped 30 of 34. Minnesota is 8-3-2 and first in the Central. Vancouver is 2-10-1 and 10 straight games without a win, and the fans booing the guy who left might want to save some for the team that stayed.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, October 25

Game recap

ANA5PHI4Final: ANA 5, PHI 4

Philadelphia built a 2-0 lead at home and then gave it away like free T-shirts. Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone scored on first-period power plays, Trevor Zegras set up both, and Tyson Foerster's shorthanded goal even had the Flyers ahead 3-2 in the second. Then Anaheim scored three straight: Judd Caulfield tied it late in the second, Tristan Luneau put the Ducks ahead two minutes into the third, and Beckett Sennecke made it 5-3 on the power play. Michkov's second of the night pulled Philly within one with almost 12 minutes left, and that was all. Luneau finished with a goal and two assists, Leo Carlsson a goal and an assist, and A.J. Greer scored, fought Hunter McDonald and piled up 17 penalty minutes. Lukas Dostal made 28 saves on 32 shots; Joseph Woll stopped 21 of 26. The Flyers are 3-7-3, and their plan for protecting a lead still looks like it was drawn on a napkin.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK1NJD3Final: LAK 1, NJD 3

The Kings went to New Jersey and put 13 shots on goal in 60 minutes, which is less an offense than a rumor. Somehow they still led: Scott Laughton scored at 15:57 of the second. It lasted 2:46, until Anthony Mantha tied it before the intermission. Brett Pesce's first goal of the season put the Devils ahead midway through the third, and Arseny Gritsyuk hit the empty net with Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt on the assists. Jake Allen had about as quiet a night as an NHL goalie gets, 12 saves on 13 shots, while Anton Forsberg stopped 23 of 25 to keep Los Angeles close. New Jersey is 7-4-0. The Kings are 2-5-2, and the shot clock in Newark barely needed batteries.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS4BOS6Final: SJS 4, BOS 6

For 48 minutes San Jose looked like it might steal one in Boston. Then the Bruins scored three goals in 3:33. Casey Mittelstadt opened it, Michael Misa answered on the power play, Marat Khusnutdinov and Kiefer Sherwood (shorthanded) traded goals in the second, and Dmitry Orlov's power-play goal gave the Sharks a 3-2 lead early in the third. David Pastrnak tied it at 8:27, James Hagens scored 40 seconds later, and Fraser Minten made it 5-3 on the power play. Will Smith pulled San Jose within one, and Will Borgen sealed it into the empty net with 28 seconds left. JJ Peterka had two assists. Jeremy Swayman made 23 saves on 27 shots; Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 29 of 34. There were two fights, Michael Kesselring with Mark Kastelic and Tanner Jeannot with Zack Ostapchuk. Boston is 9-2-1. The Sharks are 6-5-1 and learned that a third-period lead in Boston has a shelf life of about four minutes.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR4OTT7Final: NYR 4, OTT 7

Drake Batherson had a hat trick, and the Rangers' defense held the door for most of it. Ottawa led 2-0 seven minutes in on goals by Batherson and Tim Stützle, and 3-0 when Batherson scored again early in the second. New York made a game of it: Will Cuylle scored shorthanded, and after Dylan Cozens's first of the season, J.T. Miller and Alexis Lafrenière, with his ninth, made it 4-3 at the second intermission. Jake Sanderson, who finished with a goal and two assists, restored the two-goal lead, Pavel Dorofeyev pulled the Rangers within one with 4:28 left, and then the empty net did the rest: Michael Amadio, with Jonas Johansson credited with an assist, and Batherson with 12 seconds left for the hat trick. Johansson made 24 saves on 28 shots; Dylan Garand stopped 17 of 22. Ottawa is 8-4-0. The Rangers are 7-5-1, and Mike Sullivan spent the night shuffling his lines like a dealer who knows the deck is short.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH2PIT3OTFinal: NSH 2, PIT 3 OT

Nashville was 66 seconds from a win in Pittsburgh and still left with just one point. Steven Stamkos opened the scoring in the first, Connor Dewar tied it 18 seconds into the second, and Jayden Struble's first of the season put the Predators back in front. Juuse Saros held that lead until 18:54 of the third, when the Penguins pulled Arturs Silovs and Rickard Rakell scored with Sidney Crosby and Erik Karlsson on the assists. Ville Koivunen ended it 3:44 into overtime. Saros made 34 saves on 37 shots and deserved better; Silovs stopped 24 of 26. Pittsburgh is 5-6-1. The Predators are 3-3-4, and four overtime and shootout losses in 10 games means they're collecting consolation points like participation medals.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3WSH4OTFinal: BUF 3, WSH 4 OT

Buffalo went up 2-0 in Washington on goals by Jack Quinn and Josh Doan in the first 11 minutes, and you can guess the rest. Alex Tuch got one back before the first intermission, and Dylan Strome scored twice in the second to put the Capitals ahead. Noah Ostlund tied it early in the third, with Rasmus Dahlin on the assist, and that held until Tuch beat Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen 3:42 into overtime, Strome and Jakob Chychrun assisting. Jordan Kyrou had two assists. Luukkonen made 30 saves on 34 shots; Charlie Lindgren stopped 18 of 21. Washington is 6-4-0. The Sabres are 4-4-3, and blowing a two-goal lead is about the most Buffalo way there is to collect a point.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK1CBJ2OTFinal: VGK 1, CBJ 2 OT

The goalies ran this one. Denton Mateychuk put Columbus ahead in the first, Tomas Hertl tied it late in the period, and then nobody scored for more than 40 minutes because Cam Talbot and Carter Hart wouldn't allow it. A Vegas penalty in overtime gave the Blue Jackets a power play, and Adam Fantilli needed 59 seconds to end it, Charlie Coyle and Kent Johnson assisting. Talbot made 26 saves on 27 shots; Hart stopped 18 of 20. Columbus got there on 20 shots, which is efficient if not exactly thrilling, and is 4-5-0. Vegas is 8-4-1 and found out Columbus in October is no vacation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR4STL0Final: CAR 4, STL 0

Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 24 saves for a shutout in St. Louis, and Carolina did the rest at its leisure. Nobody scored in the first, and then the Hurricanes got three in the second: Sean Walker with an extra attacker on, Jesperi Kotkaniemi 20 seconds later, and Logan Stankoven's eighth. Nikolaj Ehlers added a power-play goal early in the third. Seth Jarvis and Sebastian Aho had two assists each. Carolina outshot the Blues 39-24, and Joel Hofer's 35 saves kept it from getting ugly. The Hurricanes are 9-2-2 with 20 points. The Blues are 5-5-1 and got shut out at home on 24 shots, a tough look for a team that sells itself on working hard.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR7EDM2Final: TOR 7, EDM 2

Toronto went into Edmonton and hung seven on the Oilers, which is not a sentence anyone in Alberta enjoys reading. Jack Roslovic scored unassisted in the first, Auston Matthews and Troy Stecher scored 54 seconds apart in the second, and William Nylander added two in the third, one on the power play and one into the empty net. Zack MacEwen and Vinni Lettieri scored their first goals of the season, Lettieri's with 31 seconds left after he'd fought Connor Murphy in the second. Kirill Marchenko had two assists. Leon Draisaitl scored both Edmonton goals, each set up by Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard, which is the Oilers' whole offense in one sentence. Anthony Stolarz made 30 saves on 32 shots; Tristan Jarry stopped 25 of 30. Toronto is 7-4-2. Edmonton is 8-2-1, and McDavid and Draisaitl with no help looks a lot like every Oilers June.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL4UTA5OTFinal: TBL 4, UTA 5 OT

Tampa Bay led 3-1 in the first period and 4-2 in the second and still left Salt Lake with one point. Jake Guentzel, Pontus Holmberg and Brayden Point (on the power play, Nikita Kucherov assisting) built the early lead, and Conor Geekie made it 4-2 early in the second. Utah answered with Kailer Yamamoto, Dylan Guenther on the power play, Anders Lee and then defenseman Dmitri Simashev, who tied it late in the second and won it 1:44 into overtime. Vincent Trocheck had two assists, and Karel Vejmelka picked up one on the winner to go with 29 saves on 32 shots. Dennis Hildeby stopped 23 of 28, and Tampa played the third and overtime with 11 forwards after Zemgus Girgensons left the game. Utah is 8-4-0. The Lightning are 7-3-1 and found out a two-goal lead in the mountains thins out faster than the air.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET1CGY4Final: DET 1, CGY 4

Detroit's offense in Calgary was Andrew Copp and not much else. Joel Farabee put the Flames ahead late in the first and finished with a goal and two assists. Copp tied it early in the second, and then Calgary scored three more in the period: Zayne Parekh's first of the season on the power play, Ryan Strome, and Matvei Gridin, also on the power play, with 90 seconds left. Devin Cooley made 28 saves on 29 shots; John Gibson stopped 21 of 25. Ben Chiarot and Jake Middleton fought late in the third, by which point it was the only contest left. Calgary is 4-6-0. The Red Wings are 4-4-3, and giving up two power-play goals in one period is how a rebuild stays a rebuild.

MIN5SEA1Final: MIN 5, SEA 1

Saturday, October 24

Game recap

MTL4CHI1Final: MTL 4, CHI 1

Connor Bedard scored 4:23 in, set up by Patrick Kane, and for about 13 minutes the United Center got to feel like the rebuild was over. Then Jake Evans happened. The Canadiens' checking center, not exactly the name on anyone's jersey, scored twice and added an assist, tying it late in the first and then going in shorthanded in the second, the kind of goal that should come with a refund for the Chicago power play. Kaiden Guhle made it 3-1 with 94 seconds left in the middle frame, Mike Matheson buried the empty-netter, and Montreal won 4-1 to move to 5-3-2. Jacob Fowler stopped 20 of 21 and spent most of the night watching. Spencer Knight made 24 saves on 27 shots, and Chicago managed 21 shots all game, which is about how many draft lottery balls it's been chasing since 2023. Now 3-7-0: Chicago keeps buying the rebuild, and the house keeps winning.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL3COL6Final: TBL 3, COL 6

Tampa Bay walked into Ball Arena with one of the East's best records and was down 3-0 before the second period was half a minute old. Devon Toews scored 68 seconds in, Nazem Kadri added a power-play goal, and Fedor Svechkov scored 24 seconds into the second, which is roughly how long Andrei Vasilevskiy looked comfortable all night: 18 saves on 23 shots. Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists because of course he did, Martin Necas had a goal and two helpers including the empty-netter, and Artturi Lehkonen picked up his ninth. Jake Guentzel scored twice, once on the power play, and Charle-Edouard D'Astous got it to 5-3 late, but Mackenzie Blackwood made 31 saves on 34 shots and the Lightning never got closer than two in the last 50 minutes. Colorado wins 6-3 and moves to 6-4-1. Tampa drops to 7-3-0 and flies to Utah tonight, where at least the altitude is lower.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Friday, October 23

Game recap

NSH0BOS6Final: NSH 0, BOS 6

Boston hosted Nashville and ran the Predators out of TD Garden 6-0. David Pastrnak had two goals and two assists, Charlie McAvoy set up four, and Michael DiPietro stopped all 28 shots for the shutout. Casey Mittelstadt scored 3:49 in, Elias Lindholm made it 2-0 on the power play, and after Pastrnak and JJ Peterka scored in the second, Mark Kastelic and Pastrnak, again, added two more in the third. Justus Annunen saw 31 shots and let six of them in, which is not the kind of share you want. Boston is 8-2-1. Nashville went all in on winning now, and on a night Steven Stamkos and Filip Forsberg managed two shots between them, "now" looked a lot like last season.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR4TOR5Final: NYR 4, TOR 5

Toronto beat the Rangers 5-4, and the big names had nothing to do with it. Troy Stecher scored his first of the season with 28 seconds left, and the line of Brandon Duhaime, Teddy Blueger and Zack MacEwen piled up seven points, MacEwen getting two of them in 7:06 of ice time. Auston Matthews had four shots and no points. The lead changed hands like a hot potato: Kirill Marchenko's power-play goal put the Leafs up 4-3 late in the second, and Alexis Lafrenière's eighth tied it at 14:25 of the third. Adam Fox had four assists and still lost. Sergei Bobrovsky made 21 saves on 25 shots, Dylan Garand 30 on 35. The Leafs are 6-4-2, the Rangers 7-4-1. Four goals and four Fox assists, and New York still found a way to go home with nothing but a long flight.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS6OTT2Final: SJS 6, OTT 2

San Jose went to Ottawa and won 6-2, and Yaroslav Askarov is the reason. He stopped 41 of 43 shots while the Senators threw everything at him, including nine shots from Fabian Zetterlund, who got an assist for his trouble. Tim Stützle scored first, then the Sharks took over: Nolan Allan tied it in the first, then Tyler Toffoli (power play), Collin Graf (shorthanded) and Jacob Trouba scored within 4:05 of the second. Jordan Spence pulled one back in the third, then Zack Ostapchuk (shorthanded, empty net) and Ivar Stenberg (empty net) closed it. Samuel Ersson made 22 saves on 26. The Sharks are 6-4-1. Ottawa outshot the Sharks 43-26 and lost by four, which is the most Senators sentence ever written.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA1NJD4Final: ANA 1, NJD 4

New Jersey beat Anaheim 4-1, and Nico Daws barely needed to break a sweat: the Ducks managed 17 shots all night. Arseny Gritsyuk opened the scoring 4:38 in, Nico Hischier made it 2-0 on the power play 41 seconds before the first intermission, and Jesper Bratt set up both. Tim Washe got Anaheim on the board in the third, Anthony Mantha answered five minutes later, and Jack Hughes added an empty-netter to finish with a goal and an assist. Daws made 16 saves on 17 shots, Ville Husso 25 on 28. The Devils are 6-4-0. The Ducks are 4-6-0, and on a night Leo Carlsson and Cutter Gauthier combined for three shots, the rebuild's "next step" looked a lot like the last six.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA0PIT4Final: FLA 0, PIT 4

Pittsburgh shut out the Panthers 4-0, and Arturs Silovs did it on 26 saves. Nick Robertson scored twice, the second into an empty net, with Connor Dewar assisting on both. Hendrix Lapierre and Evgeni Malkin had a goal and an assist each, Malkin's coming 1:40 into the third to make it 3-0 and end the suspense. Cooper Black made 17 saves on 20 for Florida. The Penguins are 4-6-1. The Panthers are 5-4-2, and the two-time champs got blanked by a team that was supposed to be playing for lottery balls. Nothing like a trip to Pittsburgh to remind you a parade doesn't count toward the standings.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK3NYI2OTFinal: LAK 3, NYI 2 OT

Los Angeles won 3-2 in overtime on Long Island, and Darcy Kuemper got to do it all. He stopped 41 of 43 shots, then set up Brandt Clarke's winner 2:43 into overtime, a goal and an assist for Clarke on the night. Artemi Panarin had already scored twice in the first period, the second unassisted. The Islanders came back: Victor Eklund scored on the power play in the second and Matthew Schaefer tied it 7:06 into the third, his first goal of the season, on nine shots in 29:24 of ice time. Logan Stanley and Samuel Helenius dropped the gloves late in the first. Semyon Varlamov made 24 saves on 27. The Kings are 2-4-2 and will take it. The Islanders put 43 shots on net and got beaten by a goalie's assist, which is an Islanders kind of evening.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK2STL6Final: VGK 2, STL 6

St. Louis hammered Vegas 6-2, and the Blues did it from the blue line. Justin Barron had a goal and three assists, Dylan Holloway scored twice and added a helper, and Jimmy Snuggerud had a goal and an assist. Pavel Buchnevich opened it on the power play, Barron made it 2-0, and Mason McTavish's sixth restored a two-goal lead in the second. Jack Eichel pulled Vegas within one early in the third, then the Blues scored three in 7:44 and the night was over. Joel Hofer made 27 saves on 29, Adin Hill 25 on 31. The Blues are 5-4-1, the Golden Knights 8-4-0. Vegas came in looking like the best team in hockey and left looking like a $40 buffet: fine at first, regret by the third.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG2DAL3OTFinal: WPG 2, DAL 3 OT

Dallas beat Winnipeg 3-2 in overtime, and the Jets will be thinking about this one on the flight home. Stuart Skinner, minding the net while Connor Hellebuyck's holdout drags on, stopped 35 of 38 and had the Jets two minutes from a win. Gabriel Vilardi and Kyle Connor (his ninth) had turned an early Wyatt Johnston goal into a 2-1 Winnipeg lead in the second. Then Dallas pulled Jake Oettinger, and Roope Hintz tied it with the extra skater at 18:00 of the third. Hintz won it 3:47 into overtime, set up by Miro Heiskanen and Jason Robertson. Mikko Rantanen and Robertson had two assists each. Oettinger made 17 saves on 19 shots. The Stars are 6-3-1, the Jets 4-3-3. Winnipeg had 19 shots, and the best goalie in the world is still watching from home.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN1CGY2Final: MIN 1, CGY 2

Calgary beat Minnesota 2-1, and Devin Cooley stood on his head to do it: 36 saves on 37 shots. The Flames scored both their goals on the power play in the first period, Aydar Suniev 10:49 in and Joel Farabee with his first of the season at 14:06. Michael McCarron, not exactly the scorer the Wild had in mind, got one back 4:39 into the third, and that was all Minnesota could manage. Jesper Wallstedt made 20 saves on 22. The Flames are 3-6-0 and will take a win however it comes. The Wild are 6-3-2 and outshot the Flames 37-22, and Kirill Kaprizov and friends spent 60 minutes finding out Cooley's glove is bigger than the Saddledome.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR5EDM6SOFinal: CAR 5, EDM 6 SO

Edmonton beat Carolina 6-5 in a shootout, and Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl each had two goals and three assists. The Hurricanes led 4-2 after two on goals from Jackson Blake, Sebastian Aho, Seth Jarvis and Logan Stankoven. Then McDavid scored 26 seconds into the third, Draisaitl tied it on the power play, and after Juuso Välimäki put Carolina back in front at 17:20, McDavid tied it again with the goalie pulled with 1:28 left. In the shootout McDavid and Draisaitl both missed, and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, who scored his first goal of the season in the second, got the only one. Devon Levi made 22 saves on 27, Brandon Bussi 16 on 21. The Oilers are 8-1-1, the Hurricanes 8-2-2. Carolina led three times and lost, the Hurricanes' signature move, now available in October.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA3SEA5Final: UTA 3, SEA 5

Seattle beat Utah 5-3, and the Kraken's power play did the heavy lifting. Jordan Eberle opened it 3:38 in, and after Vincent Trocheck's power-play goal tied it, Matty Beniers and Brandon Montour scored on the man advantage 21 minutes apart to make it 3-1. Logan Cooley then scored twice in the first 7:42 of the third, the first on the power play, and it was 3-3. Mackie Samoskevich won it at 14:35 off a Bobby McMann feed, and Frederick Gaudreau added an empty-netter. Philipp Grubauer made 33 saves on 36, Karel Vejmelka 18 on 22. The Kraken are 7-3-1, Utah 7-4-0. The Mammoth outshot Seattle 36-22 and lost by two, proof that you can change the name, the logo and half the roster and still have a penalty kill that hands out goals like samples at Costco.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET5VAN2Final: DET 5, VAN 2

Detroit beat Vancouver 5-2, and the Canucks managed 13 shots. Lucas Raymond had two goals and an assist, and the Wings scored three times in the first 8:56: Raymond, William Wallinder, then Raymond again on the power play after Elias Pettersson had answered on Vancouver's. Michael Rasmussen and Emmitt Finnie added the rest, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored in the third. Michael Brandsegg-Nygård and Viktor Arvidsson had two assists apiece. Michal Postava and John Gibson split Detroit's net and faced 13 shots between them; Kevin Lankinen made 26 saves on 31. The Red Wings are 4-3-3. The Canucks are 2-9-1, and 13 shots is not a hockey game, it's a cry for help from a franchise that keeps telling its fans next year starts now.

Thursday, October 22

Game recap

PHI3BUF1Final: PHI 3, BUF 1

Philadelphia, the team that scored like it was paying per goal for most of October, has now won two straight, and this time it was Cole Knuble doing the damage. The kid scored his first two of the season in 10:24 of ice time, both set up by Oliver Bonk, and Trevor Zegras slipped a power-play goal in at 19:17 of the first to make it 2-0. Buffalo's lone reply was Jason Zucker's first goal of the season, on the power play at 19:25 of the second, and the hope it brought lasted 3:03 of the third, until Knuble put the two-goal cushion back. Dan Vladar stopped 27 of 28, Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen 23 of 26, and Mattias Samuelsson piled up 17 penalty minutes, a fight with Hunter McDonald included, which was about the only thing the Sabres won all night. Buffalo is 4-4-2 after losing at home to a team that had won twice all season. In Buffalo, hope isn't a strategy, it's a subscription that renews every October whether you asked for it or not.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA1OTT5Final: FLA 1, OTT 5

Brady Tkachuk came back to Ottawa in a Panthers sweater and got the script he wanted for exactly four minutes: a power-play goal at 10:00 of the first, set up by his brother Matthew, and Bokondji Imama and Hayden Hodgson dropped the gloves five seconds later to celebrate. Then the Senators scored the next five. Tim Stützle tied it on the power play, Claude Giroux and Shane Pinto made it 3-1 in the second, and Warren Foegele and Stephen Halliday finished it off in the third. Jake Sanderson had two assists, Stützle and Halliday two points each, and Ridly Greig and Sam Bennett had a fight that was the closest the third period got. Florida managed 19 shots all night: Linus Ullmark stopped 17 of 18 before leaving in the third, and Samuel Ersson stopped the only one he saw. Akira Schmid made 25 saves on 30. Florida's three-game win streak is over. The Panthers came to Ottawa to make a homecoming about Brady, and the Senators made it about 19 shots, one goal and a long, quiet flight to Pittsburgh.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Wednesday, October 21

Game recap

SJS4MTL3OTFinal: SJS 4, MTL 3 OT

The Sharks still refuse to win a hockey game in 60 minutes, and Montreal still hasn't figured out how to stop them in 61. San Jose came back from 3-1 down and won 4-3 in overtime, and it's now 5-4-1 with zero regulation wins: every W this year has needed extra time. Macklin Celebrini did the heavy lifting with two goals and an assist, opening the scoring alone in the first and burying the power-play winner 2:13 into overtime. The Habs looked comfortable after Nick Suzuki, Juraj Slafkovský and Cole Caufield each scored, then Michael Misa got his first of the season and Tyler Toffoli tied it on a power play with 8:51 left. Alex Nedeljkovic made 31 saves; Jakub Dobes stopped 26 of 30. Montreal took a two-goal lead into the third at home against a rebuilding team and still needed a ride home: the Bell Centre has seen sturdier collapses at a hot-dog stand.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL3NJD4Final: COL 3, NJD 4

New Jersey threw Jake Allen a party for his 500th NHL game, then nearly let Colorado crash it. The Devils led 4-1 with under four minutes left after Luke Evangelista, Declan Chisholm (his first of the year), Arseny Gritsyuk and an empty-netter from Jesper Boqvist, set up by Connor Brown in his season debut. Then Artturi Lehkonen scored twice, the second with five seconds left and Scott Wedgewood on the bench, and the Prudential Center got a little sweatier than it needed to. Allen made 31 saves on 34 shots; Wedgewood stopped 37 of 40 on the second night of a back-to-back. Colorado scores more than anybody not named Edmonton, but it's now lost two straight and spent most of this one waiting for its offense to clock in: a 4.10-goals-a-game team that remembered with 3:13 to go.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA2NYI3Final: ANA 2, NYI 3

The Islanders did all their work in one first period and spent the next 40 minutes guarding it like a parking spot on Long Island. Ondrej Palat, rookie Victor Eklund and Simon Holmstrom on the power play scored in a span of 5:05, with Frank Vatrano squeezing one in between for Anaheim, and that was enough. Alex Killorn made it 3-2 with the goalie pulled and 2:40 left, but the Ducks ran out of clock. Ilya Sorokin saw just 17 shots and stopped 15; Lukas Dostal made 22 saves on 25. A.J. Greer and Mitchell Chaffee dropped the gloves in the second, which was the most Anaheim had going in the middle frame. The Ducks have now lost four straight, two at home and two in New York, and at 4-5 the road trip is turning into a long flight with a hockey problem.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK5WSH2Final: LAK 5, WSH 2

Somebody alert the Kings' equipment staff: they finally get to pack a win. Los Angeles, the league's last winless team, fell behind 2-0 in Washington on goals from Ryan Leonard and Cole Hutson, then scored twice in the final 33 seconds of the first period, Adrian Kempe and an unassisted Artemi Panarin with two seconds on the clock. Erik Gustafsson's power-play goal put them ahead in the third, Kempe added his second, and Scott Laughton hit the empty net for 5-2. Panarin finished with a goal and two assists. Darcy Kuemper made 30 saves on 32 shots against his old team; Logan Thompson stopped 21 of 25. The Kings lost Quinton Byfield early to an upper-body injury. The Capitals gift-wrapped a season's first win for a team that had scored two goals a game, which is a lovely gesture, if not one their fans asked for.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR6CBJ2Final: TOR 6, CBJ 2

Kirill Marchenko came back to Columbus wearing the other sweater and scored on his old team, which is the kind of reunion Blue Jackets fans did not RSVP for. Jake Christiansen gave Columbus a 1-0 lead 2:38 in, and then Toronto scored six of the next seven. Marchenko's power-play goal tied it, and William Nylander, Auston Matthews, Easton Cowan (short-handed) and Jack Roslovic made it 5-1 by the middle of the second. Jet Greaves was pulled after five goals on 19 shots; Cam Talbot stopped two of three. Marshall Rifai scored his first of the season in the third, and Morgan Rielly had three assists. Anthony Stolarz made 35 saves on 37. Zack MacEwen and Erik Gudbranson fought in the second. Columbus has lost two straight and now gets to watch the guy it traded light up its own building: the Blue Jackets keep making the trade, and Toronto keeps cashing it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG1STL2Final: WPG 1, STL 2

Joel Hofer turned the Enterprise Center into a no-fly zone. The Blues goalie stopped 32 of 33 shots, and St. Louis beat Winnipeg 2-1 with exactly enough offense to qualify. Jimmy Snuggerud scored in the first off a Dylan Holloway feed, Cole Perfetti tied it 32 seconds into the third, and Philip Broberg won it on the power play at 8:47. Stuart Skinner was good for the Jets too, 26 saves on 28, but he's minding the net while the actual starter's holdout suspension reportedly runs out Friday, and nobody in Winnipeg can say what happens after Friday. Kyle Connor and company managed one goal on 33 shots and dropped a third straight game. The Jets keep leaning on whichever goalie is in the building, and the offense keeps leaving them hanging, like a team still waiting for a phone call.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS2DAL3OTFinal: BOS 2, DAL 3 OT

Mikko Rantanen decided Boston's five-game winning streak had gone on long enough. He scored all three Dallas goals, the last on the power play 3:52 into overtime, and the Stars won 3-2. The Bruins led twice, on Matthew Poitras 2:09 in and rookie James Hagens in the second, and Rantanen answered both times, tying it with 6:22 left in regulation off a Roope Hintz feed. Jason Robertson had two assists. Jake Oettinger stopped 18 of 20 on a quiet night; Jeremy Swayman made 22 saves on 25. Boston still banks a point and stays first in the Atlantic at 7-2-1, but giving Rantanen and Miro Heiskanen a power play in overtime is the hockey version of leaving your keys in the car: you get exactly what you'd expect.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN3EDM4OTFinal: MIN 3, EDM 4 OT

Rule one against Edmonton: don't take penalties. Minnesota took them anyway, and the Oilers scored three power-play goals, the last one Evan Bouchard's winner 3:32 into overtime. Joel Eriksson Ek put the Wild up early, then Leon Draisaitl scored on the power play three seconds before the first intermission and again 63 seconds into the second, both set up by Connor McDavid. Mathieu Joseph made it 3-1. Minnesota came back in the third: Kirill Kaprizov scored his league-leading 11th and Ryan Hartman tied it with 6:53 left. McDavid finished with three assists. Devon Levi made 27 saves on 30; Jesper Wallstedt stopped 28 of 32. The Wild earned the point with a gutsy comeback, then handed McDavid a 4-on-3 in overtime, which is like rallying to tie a poker game and then showing the table your cards.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET3SEA4SOFinal: DET 3, SEA 4 SO

Seattle built a 3-0 lead, watched it vanish in the third period, and still went home happy after a shootout. Mackie Samoskevich, Ryker Evans on the power play and Brandon Montour, in his return, put the Kraken up three after 40 minutes. Then Detroit woke up: Viktor Arvidsson and Lucas Raymond scored 59 seconds apart early in the third, and Alex DeBrincat tied it with 17 seconds left on a power play with the goalie pulled. Overtime settled nothing, and in the shootout Frederick Gaudreau and Bobby McMann scored for Seattle while Dylan Larkin missed the last Red Wings attempt. Philipp Grubauer made 22 saves on 25; Daniil Tarasov stopped 24 of 27. The Red Wings showed real fight to steal a point, then handed the extra one back in the skills competition: 3-3-3 after nine games, Detroit has turned "almost" into a lifestyle.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR6VAN3Final: CAR 6, VAN 3

When Nicolas Deslauriers scores twice in one night, you know it's going badly for the other team. Carolina beat Vancouver 6-3, and the Canucks' fourth-line problem was a Hurricanes enforcer who now has two goals this season, both last night, including the go-ahead goal early in the third. The game was 3-3 after two, with Linus Karlsson, Jonathan Lekkerimäki and Max Sasson answering every Carolina goal. Then Deslauriers, Nikolaj Ehlers and Logan Stankoven (into the empty net) pulled away, and Ehlers and Stankoven finished with two goals each. Jackson Blake had three assists, and Juuso Välimäki assisted in his Hurricanes debut, his first NHL game in 632 days. Leevi Meriläinen faced 43 shots and made 38 saves; Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 14 of 17. Vancouver is 2-8-1 and -18, and losing a third period to Deslauriers is rock bottom with a basement under it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL6VGK2Final: TBL 6, VGK 2

Nikita Kucherov walked into Vegas three points shy of Steven Stamkos's Lightning record and walked out tied with him at 1,137. He had two assists and an unassisted third-period goal in a 6-2 rout. The first period was a fair fight: Brandon Hagel on the power play and John Carlson for Tampa Bay, Ivan Barbashev and a short-handed Mark Stone for Vegas. Then the Lightning scored four straight: Anthony Cirelli twice in the second, Victor Hedman alone late in the period, and Kucherov's milestone goal. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 32 saves on 34. Carter Hart faced 21 shots and stopped 15. Vegas came in with the league's best goal difference and spent the night getting dealt a bad hand at home: the house usually wins in this town, but last night the house got cleaned out.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Tuesday, October 20

Game recap

ANA2NYR5Final: ANA 2, NYR 5

The Rangers keep treating Madison Square Garden like a members-only club, and Anaheim wasn't on the list: 5-2, and New York is 6-0 at home. Sean Durzi scored 78 seconds in, J.T. Miller added a power-play goal, Gabe Perreault made it 3-0, and Oliver Bjorkstrand scored twice in barely 12 minutes of ice time, the kind of efficiency Rangers fans usually only see at the ticket office. Alexis Lafrenière set up two, and Dylan Garand stopped 29 of 31 to keep the Shesterkin-less crease humming. Ville Husso made 25 saves on 30. The Ducks finally scored at 18:51 of the third, then again at 19:27 through A.J. Greer, two goals that changed nothing but the box score. That's three straight losses for Anaheim, a team that flew across the country to watch a show and forgot it was supposed to be in it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL2PHI3Final: COL 2, PHI 3

Philadelphia scores 1.40 goals a game, so naturally it hung three on one of the highest-scoring teams in the league. Flyers 3, Avalanche 2, and that's two wins in three nights for a team that couldn't buy one for two weeks. Matvei Michkov scored twice, the first on the power play, and Trevor Zegras set up all three Flyers goals, including Noel Acciari's first of the season early in the third. Joseph Woll stopped 24 of 26, which is all Colorado managed to throw at him, and Nathan MacKinnon went 24 minutes without a point. Martin Necas and T.J. Hughes scored for the Avs, Hughes with five minutes left, but Mackenzie Blackwood (21 saves on 24) got no more help. A Philly lineup missing Tippett, Konecny and York did this. Colorado now flies to New Jersey to play again tonight, which is still a better trip than the one its offense just took.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS1TOR3Final: SJS 1, TOR 3

The Maple Leafs finally stopped the bleeding, and it took a teenager to do it. Toronto beat San Jose 3-1 to end a three-game skid. Mason Marchment put the Sharks up in the first, Auston Matthews tied it on the power play with 12 seconds left in the second, and Gavin McKenna scored the winner on another power play early in the third, his third of the year. Nick Paul hit the empty net with 40 seconds left. Matthews finished with a goal and two assists, William Nylander shook off an illness to set up the winner, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 30 of 31. Yaroslav Askarov was excellent in a losing cause, 29 saves on 31, and Macklin Celebrini put five shots on goal for nothing. The Sharks are 4-4-1 and still haven't won a game in regulation: nine games in, and they're still waiting for a win that doesn't need extra time or a skills competition.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT4UTA5Final: PIT 4, UTA 5

Erik Karlsson finally scored a goal, and Pittsburgh still found a way to lose. His power-play goal 71 seconds in was his first of the season, and the Penguins promptly gave up five of the next six as Utah won 5-4. Clayton Keller, Kevin Stenlund, Nate Schmidt, Kailer Yamamoto and Nick Schmaltz scored for Utah, Schmaltz on the power play early in the third for a 5-2 lead. Then the Penguins remembered they had shooters: Egor Chinakhov and Declan Carlile made it 5-4 with five minutes left, and that was it. Utah outshot Pittsburgh 29-19, so Sebastian Cossa only had to stop 15 of 19, while Arturs Silovs made 24 saves on 29. Bryan Rust had two assists before leaving with a lower-body injury. That's four straight losses and a 3-6-1 record for a team built to squeeze one more run out of Sid and Geno, and so far the only thing it's squeezing is the panic button.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, October 19

Game recap

CBJ1MIN2Final: CBJ 1, MIN 2

Columbus came to St. Paul, put 14 shots on goal in 60 minutes and somehow left with a 2-1 loss instead of a shutout, which tells you everything about Cam Talbot. Talbot stopped 32 of 34 and kept a lopsided night close. Danila Yurov opened it with 1:48 left in the first, Adam Fantilli answered a minute later with Talbot pulled for an extra attacker, and then Kirill Kaprizov did the Kaprizov thing on the power play 3:06 into the second: his 10th of the season, most in the league. After that, nobody scored for 37 minutes and Jesper Wallstedt got through his 13 saves without breaking a sweat. Minnesota is 6-2-1, in first place in the Central, and doing it without Brock Faber, Jared Spurgeon or either Foligno in the lineup. Columbus is 3-4-0 and averaged a shot every four minutes and change. You can't score on chances you don't take, and the Blue Jackets aren't taking any.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR2CGY3Final: CAR 2, CGY 3

Carolina rolled into Calgary on a seven-game win streak and ran into a team that had won once all season. The Flames won 3-2, only their second win of the season. Jesperi Kotkaniemi opened the scoring in the second, Matvei Gridin tied it with his first of the season, and Morgan Frost put Calgary ahead on the power play with 21 seconds left in the period. Jalen Chatfield tied it again with four seconds left, because the second period apparently had a closing-time rush. Then Yegor Sharangovich won it at 15:32 of the third, with Frost picking up his second point. Devin Cooley made 34 saves on 36 shots, Brandon Bussi 31 on 34, and Nicolas Deslauriers, a late call into the lineup, set up the first goal. Carolina is still 7-2-1 and first in the Metro. Calgary is 2-6-0, and one win over a good team doesn't make a rebuild, it just makes Monday less painful.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, October 18

Game recap

NJD2WSH4Final: NJD 2, WSH 4

New Jersey led for about six minutes, which is about as long as anything good lasts in Jersey traffic. Arseny Gritsyuk opened the scoring in the first, Ryan Leonard tied it on the power play (Logan Thompson picked up an assist, because why not), and then Washington scored three times in the first 11:14 of the second: Ilya Protas off an Alex Ovechkin feed, Dylan Strome, and Boone Jenner. Vincent Desharnais, not a name that usually shows up in a box score, had two assists. Thompson stopped 29 of 31; Jake Allen saw 25 shots and let in four. Timo Meier finally got his first of the season on a power play with 19 seconds left, the hockey version of finding a twenty in the couch after the rent bounced. The Devils are 4-4-0, and Jack Hughes' night was four shots, no points and 38% on draws. Somebody check whether the Devils' top line made the flight.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR3WPG2Final: CAR 3, WPG 2

Nothing hurts quite like a former Jet beating you on your own power play. Winnipeg led twice in the second, on a Mark Scheifele solo goal and Alex Iafallo off an Adam Lowry feed, and Carolina answered both: Mark Jankowski on the power play (his sixth already, so somebody alert the scouts) and Jesperi Kotkaniemi with his first of the season. Then, 6:43 into the third, Nikolaj Ehlers buried the power-play winner, set up by Shayne Gostisbehere, who had two assists. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 21 saves on 23 shots. Clay Stevenson was the busy one in the other crease, 34 saves on 37, which is what happens when your Vezina goalie is still holding out. Carolina is 7-1-1 and has won seven straight. Winnipeg is 4-2-2, and every night Hellebuyck stays away the Jets' goalie budget looks a little more like a coupon book.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2TBL4Final: VAN 2, TBL 4

Vancouver led 2-0 in Tampa, which is a sentence that should come with a warning label. Linus Karlsson scored in the first and Elias Pettersson added one on the power play early in the second, and then Nikita Kucherov decided he'd seen enough. He scored on the power play two minutes later and again at 11:23 to tie it, moving into a tie with Marian Hossa for 65th on the NHL's career points list. Jake Guentzel put Tampa Bay ahead 2:04 into the third and Pontus Holmberg added insurance on his own. Dennis Hildeby got the win with 12 saves on 14 shots, a light shift by any standard. Kevin Lankinen made 31 saves and still lost. The Lightning are 6-2-0. The Canucks are 2-7-1, and a 2-0 lead in their hands is less a cushion than a countdown.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA3FLA8Final: SEA 3, FLA 8

Two hat tricks in one night, and Seattle paid for every hat. Carter Verhaeghe scored three times in a span of 8:06 across the first and second periods, and Sam Bennett bookended the night with three of his own, in only 12:25 of ice time. Matthew Tkachuk had three assists, brother Brady had two, and Niko Mikkola and Sam Reinhart chipped in a goal and an assist each, because by the second period everyone in red was getting a turn. Florida scored twice on the power play and outshot Seattle 37-23. Joey Daccord faced all 37 and stopped 29; Jacob Markstrom made 20 saves. Shane Wright, Frederick Gaudreau and Ryker Evans scored for the Kraken, and rookie Berkly Catton had two assists. Florida is 5-2-2. Seattle is 5-3-1 and leaves South Florida with the kind of souvenir nobody wants: eight goals against and a pile of hats.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI4TOR1Final: NYI 4, TOR 1

Ilya Sorokin walked into Scotiabank Arena and turned it into a library. He stopped 28 of 29 shots, the only one that got by him a Colton Sissons goal early in the third that briefly made it 2-1. Anthony Duclair opened the scoring in the first, Bo Horvat made it 2-0 late in the second, and Simon Holmstrom scored twice in the third, the second into an empty net. Horvat had a goal and an assist and played 24:21, and Matthew Schaefer picked up another helper. Sergei Bobrovsky allowed three goals on 19 shots. Auston Matthews' six-game point streak is over, and so, apparently, is Toronto's interest in winning: the Leafs have lost five of their last six and sit at 3-4-2. The Islanders are 4-3-1. In Toronto, the October panic is right on schedule, which is more than the offense can say.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3MTL4OTFinal: BUF 3, MTL 4 OT

Buffalo keeps coming to Montreal to donate points past regulation. Josh Norris put the Sabres up in the first, then Zachary Bolduc (power play), Cole Caufield and Alexandre Texier, with his first of the season, made it 3-1 Montreal. Jack Quinn scored shorthanded and Tage Thompson tied it midway through the third, which for one shining moment looked like character. Then Caufield needed 54 seconds of overtime to score his second of the night and the 14th overtime winner of his career. Alexandre Carrier and Juraj Slafkovsky had two assists each, Jacob Fowler made 23 saves, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 30. Oliver Kapanen and David Reinbacher made their season debuts for the Canadiens. Montreal is 4-3-1. Buffalo is 4-3-2, has now lost to the Habs in a shootout and in overtime this season, and is getting really good at almost.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS3DET4SOFinal: SJS 3, DET 4 SO

San Jose has found a brand-new way to lose, and it's the same way as last game. The Sharks led 3-1 in the third on goals from Dmitry Orlov (power play), Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg (power play), with Celebrini piling up three points, his 23rd three-point game, the eighth player in NHL history with that many before turning 21. Emmitt Finnie got one back, and then Alex DeBrincat tied it 6-on-5 with 1:33 left: the second straight game the Sharks gave up a tying goal with the other goalie on the bench. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal of the shootout. John Gibson made 31 saves, Alex Nedeljkovic 24, and Keegan Kolesar and Barclay Goodrow fought in the first. Detroit is 3-3-2. The Sharks are 4-3-1, and their late-game defense is less a shell than a welcome mat.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT1PHI3Final: OTT 1, PHI 3

Somebody tell Broad Street to stop holding its breath: the Flyers have won a hockey game. Ten games in, Philadelphia got its first win of the season, and the kids did it. Drake Batherson gave Ottawa a 1-0 lead early in the second, then rookie Porter Martone tied it off a Matvei Michkov feed, and Michkov returned the favour on the power play late in the period, each finishing with a goal and an assist. Trevor Zegras iced it into an empty net with 14 seconds left. Dan Vladar stopped 25 of 26, and Linus Ullmark made 25 saves on 27 in the loss. Ottawa lost Thomas Chabot to an upper-body injury after the second period. The Flyers are 1-6-3 and the parade route is being drawn up as we speak. The Senators are 6-3-0 and just lost to the only team that hadn't beaten anybody.

Game recap

NYR0CBJ1OTFinal: NYR 0, CBJ 1 OT

Sixty minutes, zero goals, and somehow the most exciting thing in Columbus was the goaltending. Jet Greaves stopped all 29 Rangers shots for the shutout, and Dylan Garand matched him save for save until overtime, finishing with 28 on 29. Then, 3:26 into the extra frame, Kent Johnson finished it off a Zach Werenski and Charlie Coyle setup for his fourth goal of the season, and the Blue Jackets got two points out of a game that had all the scoring of a Tuesday afternoon board meeting. Columbus is 3-3-0 and gets right back at it in Minnesota tonight. The Rangers are 6-3-1, and 29 shots without a goal is the kind of night that makes a Broadway crowd start booing the Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL4CHI0Final: DAL 4, CHI 0

Jake Oettinger has now posted three shutouts before Halloween, and Chicago was happy to help. He stopped all 19 shots, which works out to roughly one every three minutes, a pace that let him plan his week between saves. Jason Robertson opened the scoring on a power play in the second, off a Mikko Rantanen feed, and added an assist. Arttu Hyry scored twice, once in the second and again 1:27 into the third, in only 12 minutes of ice time, and Roope Hintz finished it off. Spencer Knight made 28 saves on 32 and deserved a better team in front of him. Kevin Korchinski watched from the press box again. Dallas is 4-3-1. The Blackhawks are 3-6-0, and Chicago keeps buying the rebuild while the house keeps winning.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL2NSH5Final: STL 2, NSH 5

Nashville finally remembered it has a couple of very expensive forwards. Philip Broberg gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead early, Jonathan Marchessault tied it with an extra attacker on, and Filip Forsberg scored his first of the season off a Steven Stamkos feed. Adam Edstrom scored shorthanded in the second, Jimmy Snuggerud answered on the power play 31 seconds later, and then Ryan O'Reilly and Jack Drury pulled away in the third. Stamkos, Roman Josi and Adam Wilsby had two assists apiece, and Forsberg had a goal and an assist. Juuse Saros made 24 saves on 26. Jordan Binnington allowed five on 24 and played like a man counting down to the bus. Nashville is 3-2-3. The Blues are 3-4-1, and their defense spent the night giving Music City the kind of encore nobody paid for.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS4LAK1Final: BOS 4, LAK 1

The Kings scored 31 seconds in, and for the next 22 minutes, Los Angeles believed. Alex Laferriere finished off an Adrian Kempe and Brandt Clarke play, and then Boston did what Boston has been doing all week. David Pastrnak tied it on his own early in the second, Marat Khusnutdinov broke the tie with 6:24 left in the third, and Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka put two into the empty net. Pastrnak and Khusnutdinov had a goal and an assist each, and Jeremy Swayman stopped 25 of 26. Anton Forsberg made 24 saves on 26. Mark Kastelic and Samuel Helenius fought late in the first. Boston is 7-2-0 with five straight wins and a sweep of the California trip. The Kings are 0-4-2, six games without a win, and the only thing Hollywood has scripted worse this fall is a sequel nobody asked for.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM6UTA2Final: EDM 6, UTA 2

Connor McDavid scored 40 seconds in and then spent the rest of the night making Utah's defense look like it was skating in sand. He finished with two goals and three assists, stretching his season-opening point streak to eight games and his league-leading total to 23 points; his assists tie Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux for the most through a player's first eight games. Zach Hyman scored on the power play in his first game back, and Mathieu Joseph, Kasperi Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl made it 5-0 before the second period was over. Karel Vejmelka was pulled after five goals on 17 shots, and Sebastian Cossa came in. Tristan Jarry stopped 26 of 28; John Marino and Mikhail Sergachev scored in the third. Trent Frederic and Jack McBain fought. Edmonton is 6-1-1. Utah is 6-3-0, and its three-game win streak just met the one thing in hockey that doesn't care about your streak.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT2VGK6Final: PIT 2, VGK 6

Jack Eichel played his 700th NHL game and celebrated by setting up two goals before Pittsburgh had found its skates. Rasmus Andersson scored at 1:06 and Noah Hanifin at 4:02, both from Eichel and Mark Stone, and Stone added a power-play goal of his own late in the first, finishing with three points. Rookie Trevor Connelly scored on a breakaway, his fourth goal, and now leads all NHL rookies in goals and points. Shea Theodore and Brett Howden, into an empty net, rounded it out. Sidney Crosby scored on the power play and Evgeni Malkin added another, so the two franchise icons did all the scoring while the rest of the roster watched. Adin Hill stopped 22 of 24; Sergei Murashov allowed five on 19. Jeremy Lauzon and Declan Carlile fought early. Vegas is 8-2-0. Pittsburgh is 3-5-1, and Vegas just reminded the Penguins that the house always wins.
